subject: Re: MAP milestones & platform fee — Acme private pilot
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Carol Jones <carol.jones@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + platform fee proposal for Acme private pilot

Carol —

Thanks for the time this morning. Per our conversation, attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) that ties the evaluation milestones to commercial checkpoints and the proposed platform fee structure for the Private/VPC pilot. High level:

- Pilot scope: 6-week private deployment on customer VPC (staging + one production slice)
- MAP milestones: environment delivery, ingest & eval set, quality gate at week 3, scale/ramp decision at week 5
- Commercial checkpoints: initial pilot credit (non-recoupable), platform fee during pilot, ramp commitment triggers discounts and platform fee reductions

See attached: Acme_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (sheet 1 = timeline & deliverables; sheet 2 = pricing triggers). Also included Redwood_Quote_ACME_vPILOT.pdf with a line-item for the platform fee.

Open items where we need Acme confirmation:
1) Which evaluation subset will be the canonical quality gate? (you mentioned the assembly-line OCR set)
2) Procurement lead for PO/contract signature and timing
3) Desired ramp bands (we proposed 25/50/100k tokens/day)

Next steps: if procurement signs off on the MAP by close of week, we can lock the pilot price and schedule a kickoff for Sep 14.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachment: Acme_MAP_v1.2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 92 KB); Redwood_Quote_ACME_vPILOT.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)

From: Carol Jones <carol.jones@acme.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Ben Thomas <ben.thomas@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + platform fee proposal for Acme private pilot

Dylan —

Thanks for the doc and the clear plan. A couple of points from Procurement:

- The platform fee during the pilot is a sticking point. Procurement needs visibility on how that fee will be credited against future committed capacity.
- We need a clearer definition of the "quality gate" metric and a pass/fail threshold to avoid ambiguity at ramp decision time.
- PO process: we run a standard net-60 PO, and contracts will need our standard data handling addendum.

I like the MAP timeline. We can confirm the canonical eval subset by EOD Monday (I will loop in our ML ops lead).

Can your team provide an alternative commercial layout where the platform fee is partially refundable based on post-pilot committed capacity (e.g., 50% credit if ACME commits to a 12-month reserved pool within 30 days)? That would help Procurement move forward.

Appreciate it —
Carol Jones
Head of Data & Analytics | Acme Manufacturing
carol.jones@acme.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Carol Jones <carol.jones@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + platform fee proposal for Acme private pilot

Carol — Dylan —

Appreciate the feedback, Carol. We can flex the commercial layout. Suggested compromise that aligns incentives and keeps procurement comfortable:

1) Pilot platform fee: reduce the upfront platform fee by 40% for the pilot (applies to the 6-week pilot only).
2) Credit mechanism: if Acme signs a 12-month reserved capacity commitment within 30 days of successful MAP completion, 50% of the pilot platform fee is applied as a one-time credit against the first invoice of the reserved capacity term.
3) Ramp-trigger discounts: tiered discounts tied to committed throughput bands (25k/day = 5%, 50k/day = 10%, 100k/day+ = 18%). These are additive with the credit above.
4) Quality gate: define as F1 >= 0.87 on the assembly-line OCR devset and no more than 1.5% false positive delta on P0 flows. We will publish the evaluation script and seed set in the MAP doc (objective and reproducible).
5) Contracting notes: we can accept a net-60 PO for the pilot; contract will include our standard VPC security addendum and the requested data handling language.

Operational items: Monica will own the delivery of the infra checklist and runbook; Dylan will coordinate the kickoff. Monica, please confirm estimated infra lead time (we currently assume 10 business days once we have network ready).

If this works, Dylan, can you update the MAP spreadsheet to reflect these three changes and re-attach the quote with the reduced pilot platform fee? I'll also draft the credit language in plain English for Procurement to review.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Lauren / Dylan —

Thanks for adjusting the economics and for the clearer quality gate. Procurement reviewed your revised layout and are comfortable with the credit approach you described. A few final asks before we proceed to signature:

- Please provide the plain-English credit clause (Lauren mentioned she'd draft it).
- We need the updated MAP spreadsheet and revised quote reflecting the 40% reduced pilot platform fee and the credit line applied to the first reserved invoice.
- Please confirm the list of exempted data categories in the VPC security addendum (PII categories we discussed).

If those items are in place, Procurement will issue a PO (net-60) and Ben will route the contract to our legal for redlines.

We will expect the DocuSign link for signature once Redwood confirms the attachments and clause language. If possible, can we target contract signature by Sep 15 so the kickoff can proceed on Sep 21?

I'll wait for your updated files and the credit clause.

Best,
Carol Jones
Head of Data & Analytics | Acme Manufacturing
